title: Implement Phase 4A backup and crash-safe restore
scope: Deliver the first Phase 4A vertical slice: versioned directory backups of Temple project-owned canonical state, content verification, restore preview with a stale-plan digest, explicit replacement, crash-safe transactional apply, recovery rollback, and bounded audit ledgers.
acceptance_criteria: Backup creation captures the declared Temple project-owned boundary, project-owned Skills, AGENTS.md, and temple.lock while excluding generated views, runtime telemetry, managed Skill files, and application source.

Every backup records project identity, Temple version, source revision, dirty-state visibility, sorted file paths, byte sizes, modes, SHA-256 digests, exclusions, and one deterministic content digest.
Inspection rejects traversal, symlinks, extra payload files, missing files, duplicate paths, digest drift, unsupported schemas, and unsafe size or file-count bounds without mutating the project.
Restore preview reports new, identical, and replacement actions, preserved extra target files, project/version compatibility, and a deterministic plan digest without writing.
Restore apply requires the exact preview digest, refuses replacements without explicit permission, rechecks stale targets, never deletes extra project files, and rolls back ordinary failures.
An interrupted restore leaves a recoverable external ledger; recover safely restores only files still matching Temple's partial writes and refuses to overwrite subsequent human changes.
A clean-environment same-version recovery and an older-version upgrade-required rehearsal pass, generated views remain rebuildable, and no external service or credential is required.
The CLI, documentation, changelog, capability metadata, and all repository tests describe delivered behavior without claiming remote disaster recovery or distributed exactly-once execution.

required_human_approval: Project owner authorized Phase 4A implementation in this task; release is local repository state only and performs no publication or external action.
